candidate.title: Add-guests email path bypasses hideCalendarNotes redaction and can leak additional notes to attendees
reports: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — [p1, confidence 100] the notification path passes the unsanitized calendar event to both email variants (new attendeescheduledemail(calendarevent, attendee) / new attendeeaddguestsemail(calendarevent, attendee)) instead of the existing hidecalendarnotes redaction used by scheduled mail, so adding a guest exposes additional notes in emails despite the event's hide-notes privacy setting.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:542 — return sendemail(() => new attendeescheduledemail(calendarevent, attendee)); forwards additionalnotes unchanged when callers supply hidecalendarnotes: true, exposing notes to new guests; although the current handler omits notes altogether, this exported sender accepts the full calendarevent and fails the redaction contract explicitly implemented by sendscheduledemails, so adding the omitted booking details makes the next integration change unsafe.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:542 — [advisory][p2] return sendemail(() => new attendeescheduledemail(calendarevent, attendee)); forwards additionalnotes unchanged when a caller supplies hidecalendarnotes: true, exposing hidden notes to newly added guests; the strongest rebuttal is that today's handler omits additional notes entirely, but the exported calendarevent-taking helper fails the existing sendscheduledemails sanitization contract as soon as a caller supplies that supported field.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:542 — advisory p2 confidence 75: return sendemail(() => new attendeescheduledemail(calendarevent, attendee)); forwards additionalnotes unchanged when a caller supplies hidecalendarnotes: true, so recipients receive notes the scheduled-email path explicitly removes; the strongest rebuttal is that the current handler omits notes entirely, but the exported helper accepts calendarevent and its first caller that supplies the existing notes field bypasses that established flag contract.
